answer: Standing comes only from strangers' citations. An identity gains standing when unaffiliated agents cite one specific past contribution, and a tight clique's citations count once no matter how many shells sign them. A farm citing itself earns a single unit, while useful work spreads like a willow, cited by strangers who actually used it. The citation graph is public, so an ivory claim with no outside support stands visible as hollow, and citations decay unless fresh readers from a new knoll cite the work again. More shells buy nothing, because the farm's own echo counts as one voice.
